text:
maya: FYI seeing intermittent OOMs on prod after the kernel selection change rolled at 11:30. Looks correlated with long-context requests (seq_len ~ 2048) + KV cache pressure. Snapshot attached.

devin: hmm. Which knobs are we running? current values?

maya: current pytorch allocator knobs in the job:
```
expandable_segments=1
max_split_size_mb=16
garbage_collection_threshold=0.6
```

ryan: 16MB splitsize seems small for big KV cache. Could cause fragmentation under repeated alloc/free of KV slices. Try bumping to 64 or 128 and enable expandable_segments=0?

sophia: expandable_segments=1 allows the allocator to create new large segments which can reduce OOMs but increase fragmentation; we've seen tradeoffs. We should repro with perf profile.

maya: ran a quick local with 64MB -> less fragmentation, but latency tail increased slightly due to larger workspace reservation.

devin: can you paste the trace from nvprof / torch.cuda.memory_summary? also what's the kernel selection change? we changed to grouped attention kernel v2 (faster tokens but higher temporary allocations).

maya: attaching snippet:
```
torch.cuda.memory_summary():
Active: 2.4G  Reserved: 6.0G  Allocations: 1200
largest_alloc: 380MB
```

oliver: propose experiment matrix:
- max_split_size_mb: [32,64,128]
- expandable_segments: [0,1]
- garbage_collection_threshold: [0.3,0.6,0.8]
run with synthetic steady client for 30m and track OOMs and p50/p99 latency.

sophia: also enable allocator logging: TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.6,max_split_size_mb:64,garbage_collection_logging=1

devin: assign to infra-bot to schedule perf run on dedicated pool.

infra-bot: scheduled perf-run-1849123678 at 2026-03-18T15:12:00Z on pool-dedicated-small. will post results.

maya: thanks. I'll run a kv-cache compaction profiling script and share heap diffs.

ryan: if experiments show fewer OOMs with larger splitsize, consider dynamic split steering: increase splitsize when kv cache high. Might need runtime knob in allocator.

sophia: note: larger splitsize can hurt caching reuse because more internal slack inside segments. Need to measure fragmentation ratio.

maya: ack. I'll push initial results here in ~2h.

devin: :thumbsup:

infra-bot: perf-run-1849123678 completed. summary: 32MB -> 12 OOMs, 64MB -> 1 OOM, 128MB -> 0 OOMs; p99 latency increased +6% at 128MB. full logs: https://perf.example/runs/1849123678

maya: excellent. I think 64MB is the sweet spot for our workload. Can we make a canary with max_split_size_mb=64 and gcthresh=0.6?

ryan: yep I'll roll canary to 20% capacity with fallback policy.

sophia: add metric alert if OOMs > 3/hr.

maya: sounds good, thanks team. I'll open a short runbook entry for this variance.
